stories.title: Food inflation to stay elevated; ICICI Bank sees 25 bps RBI rate hike in December
stories.hook: Food inflation to stay elevated; ICICI Bank sees 25 bps RBI rate hike in December
points: Food inflation in India is projected to remain elevated in the coming months due to a shortfall in crops.
stories.summary: Food inflation in India is projected to remain elevated in the coming months due to a shortfall in crops. The Reserve Bank of India is anticipated to raise interest rates by 25 basis points to manage retail inflation. Factors such as weak monsoon and high energy prices contribute to the rising inflation. Many essential food items are experiencing upward price pressure amid ongoing inflationary trends.

stories.title: Retail inflation may remain above 6 pc for next few months; economists see possibility of rate hikes
stories.hook: Retail inflation may remain above 6 pc for next few months; economists see possibility of rate hikes
points: Mumbai's consumer price index-based retail inflation is projected to remain above 6 percent in upcoming months.
stories.summary: Mumbai's consumer price index-based retail inflation is projected to remain above 6 percent in upcoming months. This rise is attributed to increasing food prices, an adverse base effect, and commodity price impacts. Economists predict that retail inflation will average 6.2 percent in the October-December quarter of FY27. Heightened food prices and weather-related risks pose ongoing challenges for crop production.

stories.title: India needs to create high-quality jobs, increase productivity growth: IMF
stories.hook: India needs to create high-quality jobs, increase productivity growth: IMF
points: The International Monetary Fund has upgraded India's potential growth to 6.8 percent, citing favorable demographics and a growing economy.
stories.summary: The International Monetary Fund has upgraded India's potential growth to 6.8 percent, citing favorable demographics and a growing economy. Higher productivity growth and stronger private investment are essential to realize this potential. Faster creation of high-quality jobs is also crucial for sustainable economic development. The IMF continues to view India as a key growth engine for the global economy.

stories.title: World is now in ‘age of electricity’, energy agency chief says
stories.hook: World is now in ‘age of electricity’, energy agency chief says
points: Exclusive: Fossil fuels no longer dominant energy source, IEA leader says, as summit considers electrification pledge The world has left behind the age of…
stories.summary: Exclusive: Fossil fuels no longer dominant energy source, IEA leader says, as summit considers electrification pledge The world has left behind the age of coal, oil and gas and is now firmly in “the age of electricity”, the world’s leading energy economist has said. Fatih Birol, the executive director of the International Energy Agency (IEA), said more than twice as much electricity generation would be added to the global economy in the next decade than in the last, as countries scramble to secure their energy supplies against fossil fuel price volatility and supply shocks, such as the Iran war.
